Solar Open 2: Hybrid Attention and the Economics of Long-Horizon Agents

Jie Zhu · 2026-07-22 · 6 min

Reading the July 22 report through three questions: what to retain in context, how to combine specialist teachers, and how to verify real work.

A same-day technical report

Upstage announced Solar Open 2 on July 22, and the first version of its technical report was submitted to arXiv that day. This article uses that v1 rather than the later revision. The report describes a 250B-total, 15B-active MoE designed for long-horizon agent tasks and a context window reaching one million tokens.

The interesting part is the route to that capacity. The report combines a hybrid attention stack, value-focused data selection, and specialist-teacher consolidation. Read together, these choices address different bottlenecks: processing long histories, spending training compute effectively, and integrating skills needed for multi-step work.

Sources: [1]

Hybrid attention is a resource tradeoff

The v1 report interleaves one softmax-attention layer with every three linear-attention layers. It also describes a gated delta rule extended to negative eigenvalues. The architectural claim is specific; it should not be simplified into a claim that attention has become free or that any million-token input is equally useful.

My engineering reading is that context capacity and useful memory are separate properties. An agent may fit its entire history yet fail to retrieve an early requirement. I would test cross-file dependencies, constraints introduced early in a session, and distractor-heavy documents at several input lengths, while recording prefill time and peak memory.

Sources: [1]

Specialists need to become one usable policy

The report trains twelve domain specialists and combines them with Multi-teacher On-Policy Distillation. In on-policy distillation, the student's own generated trajectory determines where supervision is applied. This is different from simply collecting polished teacher answers and treating them as a static instruction dataset.

For a deployment team, the next question is skill interference. Does stronger coding preserve document extraction and tool formatting? Build a regression matrix across task families, including mixed tasks that require more than one skill. A higher average can hide a regression in the one workflow that generates most business value.

Sources: [1]

A practical acceptance test

For a document agent, ask it to extract evidence, produce a structured artifact, and then verify that artifact against source records. Keep the verifier independent from the generated explanation. Evaluate missing evidence and conflicting instructions deliberately. Upstage's launch emphasizes checking changed state after tool use; that is a useful design direction, but a private acceptance test still has to establish whether it works for your data.
